title: Question about making a sprite -sheet in Asesprite

posts.author: ANT0NS3DG3
posts.body:
I'm making a sprite sheet that uses DreamX_SideViewFrames, which means it'll have more than the standard 3 frames. In my case, I'm making an 8-frame sprite sheet.
My idea is to separate the layers based on the direction,
Down - Left - Right - Up
To match the RPG Maker MV standard, export it, then re-cut and assemble it in Photoshop using the Sprites in the Project files as templates.
Is this a good way to do it, or is there a better and easier way? Such as being able to format the sprite sheet export in Asesprite to match RPG Maker MVs?

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
I don't think you need Photoshop at all to create sprite sheets from Aseprite. That being said, I'm puzzled why you would want directions to be on separate layers. Typical workflow in Aseprite is to use draw each frame on a separate... frame (I mean that's the whole
raison d'être
of Aseprite) and then export as sprite sheet.
So in your case you would just have 8 frames of down, 8 frames of left, etc back to back for 32 frames total, and export as sprite sheet in 8 columns (or whatever format your plugin requires).
Note: please going forward include a link to the plugin, that will help in figuring out what your specific needs are.

DreamX_SideViewFrames.js
seems to be for sideview battlers...?

So once you have your export of a single sprite sheet, you can press “C” on the key board to adjust the canvas size. I’m not sure if the goombah is supposed to have just three directions, but if you need eight characters like these you’d just pad 144 to the bottom and 1152 to the right.
When copying other sprite sheets into this one, you can press
Ctrl + ^
to show the grid (should be 48 by 48) and press
Shift + S
to turn “snap to grid” on. This way you prevent misaligning as you combine the sprites.

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
Okay, I said 48 px assuming that the sprite height is 48px. If it’s not, you need to adjust the sprite sheet height accordingly.
Naturally, all the sprites on a single sheet need to be the same frame size. This has nothing to do with Aseprite or Photoshop, rather it’s planning ahead; you can’t mix sprites of different height on a single sheet and expect it to work.
The sprite height and width you can determine by dividing the pngs by the number of frames horizontally and vertically.

I don’t understand how you came to these numbers… have you reviewed the asset standards of RPG Maker? I don’t know how long you’ve been at RPG Maker, but this is pretty critical stuff to understand before delving into plugins.
The standard sheet (with eight characters) has eight frames vertically and twelve frames horizontally. Take the file’s dimensions, and divide the height by 8, and the width by 12. With the standard assets included, this is a frame size of 48px by 48px. I don’t know what format Galv uses, but I suspect it to be something similar. So if the sprite sheet from Galv’s example is, say, 480 high, the frame height would be 60. Same idea for the width.
